cultivar: Anshun local small-leaf population plants, Fuding Dabai
processing: A curled, downy maofeng green combining traditional methods with modern equipment, with the enzymes fixed by heat and no oxidation.
harvest_season: Spring. Grades run from one bud with a just-opening leaf (first grade) to one bud with two leaves and a third just opening (third grade).
appearance_dry: Fine, tight, curled strips with plenty of visible down, silvery green with a hidden jade tone.
appearance_wet: Even, very young and tender buds and leaves.
taste_profile: Fresh, mellow and clean in the mouth, with a chestnut note and more staying power over steeps than its pale colour suggests.

brewing.notes: Downy leaf can make the first steep look a little cloudy, which is normal. Its reputation is for lasting through several infusions, so do not stop after one.

vintage_note: Usual for Chinese greens: sold as the current spring harvest, by grade, and best drunk within about a year. A first-grade lot should show mostly bud and young leaf with obvious down.
description:
Huangguoshu Maofeng is a curled, downy green from the Anshun area of western Guizhou, sharing its name with the famous waterfall nearby. The protected area covers Xixiu, Pingba, Puding, Zhenning, Guanling, Ziyun and two further Anshun zones.

It was developed at a sericulture farm below Laoluopo, at about 1,365 metres, where cloud and big swings between day and night temperature favour slow bud growth. Pickers there were told to skip buds without down, overwintered buds, damaged buds and purple ones.

The local saying is that it looks like vegetable water but tastes of chestnut in the mouth, and that is a useful way to approach it: the pale liquor undersells the flavour. It tastes fresh and mellow and is known for holding up over repeat steeps. Keep the water below boiling, but give later infusions more time.

When buying, the grade tells you a lot, and the down and even size are easy things to check by eye. If you like the chestnut side of this tea, compare it with other Guizhou greens that have the same note.
history:
Anshun tea reached a high point in the 1970s, when spring tea from the Huangguoshu area earned the nickname 'MSG tea' for its savoury freshness. Accounts treat that reputation as the direct push behind creating this tea.

It was developed by prefectural agriculture bureau tea technicians and staff of the prefectural sericulture farm, after three years of feasibility work and small trial batches. At the 1994 China Tea Cup national competition its first and second grades both took top special awards in a field of 247 samples.

The national quality inspection authority approved geographical indication protection on 13 March 2012.
